teaser.text: ExxonMobil is an energy and materials company: it finds oil and gas, turns them into fuels and industrial ingredients, and sells them through a global network. A dollar reaches it when a customer buys one of those products, and leaves it again through the costs of making, moving and renewing the system.

blocks.heading: Where could ExxonMobil's shares be in each forecast year?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast puts ExxonMobil at $207.51 in October 2027, including dividends, against today’s $168.56. That is a 26% return. The weighted price reaches $221.82 in October 2028, a 37% return, and $243.08 in October 2029, a 52% return.
The October 2029 range is $122.97 to $392.14. Today’s share price is $168.56. The bear case receives 30% probability. The base case receives 55%. The bull case receives 15%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for ExxonMobil?

paragraphs.text: The base EBITDA path starts at $92 billion in October 2027 and reaches $100 billion in October 2029. The intervening value is $96 billion. The starting point is anchored to the supplied NTM EPS estimate of $11.3578, converted into roughly $47.7 billion of net income before adding estimated taxes and D&A. The path then grows as Guyana and Permian volumes rise, costs improve and chemicals recover. The bear case starts at $68 billion, falls to $65 billion, then recovers to $67 billion because weaker prices, refining margins and disruptions overwhelm volume growth. The bull case rises from $105 billion to $119 billion as production ramps, Pioneer synergies arrive and margins strengthen. ExxonMobil’s proxy fell from $101.8 billion in 2022 to $67.3 billion in 2025, supporting this wide range.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay today for ExxonMobil?

paragraphs.text: The price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, compares the share price with recent profit. A high oil price can enlarge earnings without making Exxon more productive, so a low P/E may reflect a temporary commodity surge. Normalized earnings ask what profit might look like under comparable oil prices and margins. ROCE, or return on capital employed, adds a harder test: how much operating profit the company earns from the money tied up in wells, refineries and plants. Exxon’s reported 2025 ROCE was 9.3%.

blocks.heading: How much does ExxonMobil pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Production rose to 4,736 thousand oil-equivalent barrels per day in 2025, but realized liquids prices fell to $55.30 per barrel. Capital spending reached $28,358 million and calculated net debt reached $32,856 million. Chemical earnings fell to $800 million, with chemical ROCE at 2.7%. ExxonMobil’s free cash flow per share was $6.07, against $4.00 of dividends per share. Buybacks were $4.71 per share, yet net share dilution was 0.2%.

The base dividend rises from $4.12 per share to $4.36 by October 2029. The bear case holds it at $4.12, while the bull case reaches $4.52. The latest declared quarterly dividend was $1.03, and annual DPS rose each year from 2021 through 2025. The pause protects the bear case from assuming a cut, while the increases reflect management’s stated priority of a growing dividend.

paragraphs.text: Valuation can still fall even if earnings reach the forward estimate. At a later multiple of 12x, that earnings base would value the shares at about US$136.67 before dividends. The 2.4% dividend yield offers income, but only a limited cushion against a large price decline.

earnings.opening: ExxonMobil's next results are expected on October 30, 2026. ExxonMobil's key watch is Uaru's first oil and operating ramp.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how ExxonMobil makes money, who its rivals are, how management operates and what risks it faces.

blocks.heading: What has ExxonMobil guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: “Upstream” means finding and producing oil and gas before they reach a refinery or customer. ExxonMobil guides to 4,900 thousand oil-equivalent barrels per day, including 1,800 thousand from the Permian Basin. Oil-equivalent barrels convert gas into an energy comparison with oil; they do not mean gas sells for the same price. The target is an annual average, so a strong month cannot erase earlier lost production.

Buybacks distribute cash now, while capital spending aims to create future cash. ExxonMobil’s methane-intensity promise measures emissions relative to activity against its 2016 baseline for operated assets; it does not promise an equivalent cut in every absolute emission category.

paragraphs.text: Exxon also reported $15.1 billion of structural cost savings by the end of 2025 against a target of approximately $15 billion by 2027. That supports management’s credibility, although savings remain a management-defined measure and earnings still declined as prices weakened.

blocks.heading: What do ExxonMobil's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: The June 2026 quarter delivered a sharp earnings recovery, but prices and accounting timing explain more than production growth. Production fell from 4,630 to 4,514 thousand oil-equivalent barrels a day even as revenue and profit surged.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in ExxonMobil's next results?

paragraphs.text: In the fourth quarter, investors should watch Uaru’s first oil and its operating ramp. Golden Pass LNG, developed with QatarEnergy, also matters: mechanical completion of a processing train means construction has reached a defined stage, not that commissioning, reliable operation or cargo sales have begun.
